# Arguments

The command-line arguments the process was started with.

<h2 id="argument-count"><code>ArgumentCount</code></h2>

```rux
pub func ArgumentCount() -> uint
```

How many arguments the process was started with, the program itself included.
Usually at least one, since the program is passed as the first argument; a parent may pass none at all, and then
this is zero. Cannot fail and allocates nothing.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Process/Src/Arguments.rux#L17)

**Returns**: the argument count

<h2 id="argument"><code>Argument</code></h2>

```rux
pub func Argument(index: uint) -> OsStringView?
```

The argument at `index`, counting the program as argument zero, or none past the last one.
The view borrows storage the process owns for its whole life. Cannot fail and allocates nothing.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Process/Src/Arguments.rux#L26)

**Parameters**

| Name    | Type   | Description                             |
| ------- | ------ | --------------------------------------- |
| `index` | `uint` | the zero-based position of the argument |

**Returns**: the argument's native units, or none when `index` is not below [`ArgumentCount`](/docs/api/process/arguments#argument-count)

<h2 id="argument-iterator"><code>ArgumentIterator</code></h2>

```rux
pub struct ArgumentIterator {
    // private fields
}
```

A walk over the process's arguments in order, the program first.
`Copy`; each copy walks on its own from where it was copied. Holds only a position, so it allocates nothing.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Process/Src/Arguments.rux#L34)

**Methods**

<h3 id="argument-iterator-iterate"><code>Iterate</code></h3>

```rux
pub func Iterate(self: &ArgumentIterator) -> ArgumentIterator
```

The walk itself, so that `for argument in Arguments()` reads every argument.

**Returns**: a copy of this walk from its current position

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Process/Src/Arguments.rux#L51)

<h3 id="argument-iterator-skip"><code>Skip</code></h3>

```rux
pub func Skip(
    self: &var ArgumentIterator,
    count: uint
) -> ArgumentIterator
```

Leaves out the next `count` arguments, as `Skip(1)` leaves out the program.
Advances the walk and returns it, so the call can be chained in a `for` header. Cannot fail.

| Name    | Type   | Description                     |
| ------- | ------ | ------------------------------- |
| `count` | `uint` | how many arguments to pass over |

**Returns**: this walk, advanced

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Process/Src/Arguments.rux#L60)

**Implements Iterator**

`ArgumentIterator` conforms to `Iterator`.

<h3 id="argument-iterator-next"><code>Next</code></h3>

```rux
pub func Next(self: &var ArgumentIterator) -> OsStringView?
```

The next argument, or none after the last.

**Returns**: the argument's native units, borrowing storage the process owns for its whole life

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Process/Src/Arguments.rux#L70)

<h2 id="arguments"><code>Arguments</code></h2>

```rux
pub func Arguments() -> ArgumentIterator
```

Every argument the process was started with, the program first.
Cannot fail and allocates nothing. Use `Skip(1)` on the result, or start a loop at index one, to leave out the
program's own name.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Process/Src/Arguments.rux#L43)

**Returns**: a walk over the arguments
